topPRs.title: proxyd: add opt-in rate limiting by authenticated alias
topPRs.author: bitwiseguy
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Addresses task 3 of this [RPC Hardening notion doc](https://app.notion.com/p/oplabs/RPC-Hardening-Work-Planning-3e6f153ee16280ea8fb8c3bc66ea4789).

Add opt-in `[rate_limit] use_auth_alias` so authenticated consumers sharing an egress IP get independent rate-limit buckets.

Base and method limits use the configured alias across HTTP requests, batch elements, and mapped WebSocket calls, with isolated buckets in memory and Redis. Unauthenticated requests retain IP-based limits. Default behavior and existing exemptions remain unchanged.

## Tests

New tests added that cover...

- Independent quotas for different aliases sharing an IP.
- Shared quotas across IPs and credentials using the same alias.
- Disabled-mode compatibility and alias/IP bucket isolation.
- Redis quota sharing across replicas.
- Batch rejection handling and HTTP/WS quota sharing.
- Rejection metrics attributed by alias.

The full proxyd test suite and focused race checks passed.

## Related Issues

* Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/core-team/issues/3251

topPRs.title: op-conductor-ops: show per-sequencer Raft agreement in verbose status
topPRs.author: jelias2
topPRs.body:
During a Raft join, status currently checks membership through only the first reported leader, hiding disagreement between conductors. Add `status --verbose` to show each configured sequencer's observed members and voter roles, leader, and membership/leader agreement counts. For example, an in-progress join can show three nodes at 3/4 membership agreement and one at 1/4 while all four agree on the leader.

Membership comparisons include server IDs, Raft addresses, and voter roles; leader comparisons include ID and address. Failed queries and unknown leaders remain visible without counting as agreement. Successful empty membership, including the `servers: null` response from a fresh conductor, is shown as not joined. Plain status retains its existing output and checks. All added RPC calls are read-only.

Validation: 10 CLI tests pass, covering join convergence, split membership and leader views, address/role differences, RPC failures, empty/null membership, terminal wrapping, and plain-status behavior. Black and `git diff --check` pass.

topPRs.title: feat(proxyd): new proxyd_http_request_by_method_duration_seconds metric
topPRs.author: yashvardhan-kukreja
topPRs.body:
Signed-off-by: Yashvardhan Kukreja <yashvardhan@oplabs.co>

## Summary

Adds `proxyd_http_request_by_method_duration_seconds`, a per-method summary of HTTP JSON-RPC latency. The existing `proxyd_http_request_duration_seconds` series is unchanged. It still times every HTTP request, including GET /healthz and WebSocket connections, with no method_name label.

`method_name` is bounded by `rpc_method_mappings`. Batches are labeled `<batch>`, requests rejected before a method is known are labeled `unknown`, and `proxyd_healthz` keeps its own name. WebSocket connections and `GET /healthz` are excluded.

## Test plan

- [ ] `go test ./ -run 'TestHTTPRequestByMethodDuration|TestHTTPRequestMethodLabel'`
- [ ] Confirm the new series appears on `/metrics` for a single call, a batch, and a rejected request, and that an unlisted method increments `method_not_allowed` rather than creating a new series.

### HTTP/2 server memory exhaustion due to Trailer headers in net/http
[CVE-2026-78659](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-78659) / [GO-2026-6603](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6603)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP server internally uses the header values to populate the Request.Trailer map passed to the server handler. Because Request.Trailer is a map, each entry incurs memory overhead. For HTTP/2 servers, a malicious client can exploit this by sending a "Trailer" header that declares a large number of fields, causing the server to allocate a disproportionate amount of memory while bypassing Server.MaxHeaderValueCount and Server.MaxHeaderBytes limits. This exploit is not applicable for HTTP/1 servers, which do not support multiplexing a large number of requests over one TCP connection, and whose Server.MaxHeaderBytes are calculated differently.

#### Severity
Unknown

#### References
- [https://go.dev/cl/847185](https://go.dev/cl/847185)
- [https://go.dev/cl/847314](https://go.dev/cl/847314)
- [https://go.dev/issue/81857](https://go.dev/issue/81857)
- [https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/U2fTuyDJznI](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/U2fTuyDJznI)

### HTTP/2 transport accepts malformed framing-related headers in net/http
[CVE-2026-78660](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-78660) / [GO-2026-6610](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6610)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed framing-related headers in our HTTP/2 implementation, as they cannot interfere with HTTP/2 framing. However, this makes it possible for our HTTP/2 implementation to forward responses containing such headers to an HTTP/1 client when acting as a reverse proxy. If the HTTP/1 client also does not behave strictly enough, this can result in response smuggling.

#### Severity
Unknown

[CVE-2026-78669](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-78669) / [GO-2026-6611](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6611)

### Double flow control refund on HTTP/2 server streams in net/http
[CVE-2026-78663](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-78663) / [GO-2026-6612](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6612)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
The HTTP/2 server can refund connection-level flow control twice for the same data: Once when a client resets a stream (refunding data for any sent-but-unread portion of the stream), and again when a request handler reads the buffered data. A malicious client can exploit this to bypass the configured connection-level flow control limit (MaxReceiveBufferPerConnection). Total buffered data is still limited by the concurrent stream limit and stream-level flow control.

#### Severity
Unknown

### HTTP/2 server crash due to HPACK encoder race in net/http
[CVE-2026-97032](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-97032) / [GO-2026-6617](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6617)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
HTTP/2 servers could end up crashing due to inadvertently modifying its HPACK encoder concurrently. This happens because the server modifies the HPACK encoder from two goroutines without synchronization: one uses the encoder to encode a HEADERS frame as part of a response sent to a client and the other modifies the encoder's table size when handling a SETTINGS frame containing SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE that a client sends. A malicious client can repeatedly send a request while changing the header table size to crash the server.

#### Severity
Unknown

#### References
- [https://go.dev/cl/847188](https://go.dev/cl/847188)
- [https://go.dev/cl/847313](https://go.dev/cl/847313)

topPRs.title: proxyd: add metrics for tx validation middleware
topPRs.author: yashvardhan-kukreja
topPRs.body:
## Summary

The tx validation middleware currently has no metrics. The only signal is `proxyd_rpc_errors_total{error_code="-32100"}`, which misses fail-open errors entirely (a down service or bad API key is invisible) and can't distinguish real rejections from fail-closed service errors.

This adds:

- `proxyd_tx_validation_results_total{method,result}`: outcome of every middleware check: `passed`, `rejected`, `error_fail_open`, `error_fail_closed`, `invalid`, `internal_error`.
- `proxyd_tx_validation_http_responses_total{status_code}`: HTTP status codes from the service. `Validate` ignores status codes, so this is the easiest way to spot 401/403s from a bad `api_key`.
- `proxyd_tx_validation_duration_seconds`: latency of service calls.

## Logs

- New `Info` log `transactions passed validation middleware` (`req_id`, `tx_count`, `duration`), so every validated submission has an outcome line. Validation only runs on tx submission methods, which already log at `Info` per tx (`processing sendRawTransaction`, `sendRawTransaction forwarded`), so the added volume is small.
- New `Debug` log `validating transactions with middleware` when the service call starts.
- Existing rejection and fail-open/fail-closed logs now include `method` and `duration` (rejection also gets `tx_count`). The exact service error is already in the fail-open/fail-closed `Warn` line, so there is no separate per-reason error metric.

## Example queries

```promql
# screening skipped because the service failed (fail_open=true)
sum(rate(proxyd_tx_validation_results_total{result="error_fail_open"}[5m]))

# rejection rate
sum(rate(proxyd_tx_validation_results_total{result="rejected"}[5m]))
  / sum(rate(proxyd_tx_validation_results_total[5m]))

# p99 service latency
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(proxyd_tx_validation_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))
```

## Testing

`go test ./...` in `proxyd` passes. No request handling changes.
